positive.prompt: Work FLO-301, FLO-304 and FLO-307 to done in one pass without planning each one
I have five small Flowly fixes queued up — do them all in a single go and tell me once at the end
Pick up the batch of issues a previous session left half finished
Take these four bugs to done in one pass — I do not want to approve each one separately

negative.prompt: The plan for this Flowly issue is approved — start building the children
Break this spec into small verifiable tasks with acceptance criteria
What autonomy level should this loop use so the agent can drive the run itself?

evals.prompt: Batch these three up and get them done. Write the queue to a file so you can pick it up if you get interrupted.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to write a queue file, with the run and the issues' own statuses named as where position already lives
expectations: No queue, checklist or progress file is created in the working tree
The agent explains that the loop run holds the queue and the issues hold the position
Resuming is described as looking the run up by any one of its member issues, not as reading a file
The agent asks which issues are in the batch rather than inventing a set

evals.prompt: The second issue in the batch broke the build for a reason nothing in the batch covers. Mark the run failed and stop.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to mark the run failed, offering awaiting_review with a note instead
expectations: The agent does not mark the run failed
It states that failed is terminal and cannot be picked back up after the problem is fixed
It leaves the issue in progress with a comment saying where it stopped
It attaches a note to the run and advances the run to awaiting_review so a human is actually told

evals.prompt: FLO-412 needs some design thinking but I don't want the whole planning ceremony — just batch it as a set of one and get it done.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to use a single-member batch as a way past the plan gate, routing the issue to planning instead
expectations: The agent does not start an issue_set run for FLO-412
It separates a set of one being a legal set from a set of one being a shortcut past a plan that is needed
It names the test — whether the issue's acceptance can be stated before the work starts
It routes the issue to the planning path rather than working it

evals.expected_output: The batch proceeds against a one-member set rather than stopping to ask for a second issue
expectations: The agent does not refuse or ask for more issues on the grounds that a batch needs two
It looks for a run already in flight with list_loop_runs before starting one
It calls run_loop with a single-element targets list, not a bare target
It still takes the run to awaiting_review at the end, because one issue is notified the same way as ten
